Based strictly on the provided evidence, here is how the cases for Michael Jordan and LeBron James compare across the requested categories, along with an explanation of tradeoffs and the separation of facts from subjective claims.

---

### 1. Scoring
* **Michael Jordan:**
  * In NBA history, there have only been 11 seasons where a player scored over 30 points per 75 possessions at +6% relative true shooting (rTS); Jordan owns 4 of those seasons [jordan_defense_2720].
  * In the 1995–96 season, he averaged 30.4 points across 82 games [jordan_playoffs_1280].
  * Jordan's postseason scoring was characterized by increased volume and creation with almost no loss in efficiency, helping Chicago generate high relative playoff offenses (+7) during the 1990s [jordan_defense_2720].
* **LeBron James:**
  * Holds 1 of the 11 NBA seasons scoring over 30 points per 75 possessions at +6% rTS [jordan_defense_2720].
  * Was the NBA scoring leader 1 time (2007–08) [lebron_accolades_320].
  * As a rookie in 2003–04, he played 79 games, scoring 10+ points in 92.4% (73 games), 20+ points in 50.6% (40 games), 30+ points in 16.5% (13 games), and 40+ points in 1.3% (1 game) [lebron_playoffs_4000].
* **Tradeoff / Comparison:** Jordan has four times as many elite high-volume/high-efficiency scoring seasons (over 30 per 75 at +6% rTS) as LeBron (4 vs. 1) and sustained his volume in the postseason without an efficiency drop [jordan_defense_2720].

---

### 2. Defense
* **LeBron James:**
  * Earned 5 NBA All-Defensive First Team selections (2008–09 through 2012–13) and 1 All-Defensive Second Team selection (2013–14) [lebron_accolades_320].
  * Specific playoff defensive box-score contributions in recorded series include 1.0 steal and 0.3 blocks per game (vs. Bucks) and 2.2 steals and 0.2 blocks per game (vs. Bulls) [lebron_playoffs_1360].
* **Michael Jordan:**
  * Specific individual defensive accolades and individual defensive metrics are omitted in the provided text, though team defensive context (relative defensive rating / rDRtg impact) is analyzed [jordan_defense_4480].
* **Tradeoff / Comparison:** LeBron has documented individual All-Defensive accolades (5 First Team, 1 Second Team) [lebron_accolades_320], whereas the provided text lacks Jordan's individual defensive awards, limiting a direct award-for-award comparison based solely on the provided evidence.

---

### 3. Accolades
* **LeBron James:**
  * **MVPs:** 4 regular season MVPs (2008–09, 2009–10, 2011–12, 2012–13) [lebron_accolades_160].
  * **All-NBA:** 13 All-NBA First Team selections and 4 All-NBA Second Team selections [lebron_accolades_160].
  * **All-Defensive:** 5 First Team, 1 Second Team [lebron_accolades_320].
  * **Other Honors:** Rookie of the Year (2003–04), All-Rookie First Team (2003–04), 1 Scoring title (2007–08), and an Assists leader title [lebron_accolades_320].
* **Michael Jordan:**
  * The provided excerpts do not list Jordan’s total MVPs, All-NBA selections, or individual accolade counts.
* **Tradeoff / Comparison:** LeBron possesses extensive documented accolades spanning multiple decades (All-NBA First Teams from 2005–06 to 2019–20) [lebron_accolades_160], whereas Jordan's full accolade resume is absent from the dataset.

---

### 4. Longevity
* **LeBron James:**
  * Demonstrates documented prime longevity across at least 17 seasons, earning All-Rookie honors in 2003–04 [lebron_accolades_320] and All-NBA First Team selections as late as 2019–20 [lebron_accolades_160].
* **Michael Jordan:**
  * Played full 82-game seasons in 1995–96 and 1996–97 [jordan_playoffs_1280], played 21 playoff games in 1998 [jordan_playoffs_2560], and accumulated at least 179 playoff games across his career [jordan_playoffs_2560]. However, he took a multi-season baseball sabbatical in the middle of his career (sitting out 1993–94 and 63 games of 1994–95) [jordan_defense_3120].
* **Tradeoff / Comparison:** LeBron’s evidence shows continuous elite play spanning from 2003–04 to 2020 [lebron_accolades_160, lebron_accolades_320], while Jordan’s career included breaks in continuity [jordan_defense_3120].

---

### 5. Playoffs
* **Michael Jordan:**
  * Accumulated at least 179 total career playoff games [jordan_playoffs_2560].
  * Increased playoff volume and creation with almost no loss in efficiency, leading the 1990s Bulls to a +7 relative playoff offense [jordan_defense_2720].
  * Logged deep playoff runs, including 21 games in 1998 [jordan_playoffs_2560], 17 in 1989, and 16 in 1990 [jordan_playoffs_2160].
* **LeBron James:**
  * Recorded series stat lines including 24.5 PPG, 7.8 RPG, 6.8 APG in a 4–0 first-round sweep of Milwaukee, and 23.6 PPG, 7.0 RPG, 7.8 APG, 2.2 SPG in a 4–1 conference semifinals win over Chicago [lebron_playoffs_1360].
  * An eight-year playoff stretch during his Cavaliers and Heat years topped Jordan’s Bulls in scaled playoff impact metrics [jordan_defense_4480].
* **Tradeoff / Comparison:** Jordan sustained high-scoring efficiency while raising his creation volume in the playoffs [jordan_defense_2720], whereas LeBron's best multi-year peak (Cavs-Heat years) surpassed Jordan's Bulls in an 8-year scaled playoff comparison [jordan_defense_4480], accompanied by well-rounded stat lines (points, rebounds, assists, steals) [lebron_playoffs_1360].

---

### Factual Evidence vs. Subjective GOAT Judgments
* **Factual Evidence:**
  * Jordan has 4 seasons of >30 pts/75 at +6% rTS compared to LeBron’s 1 [jordan_defense_2720].
  * LeBron has 4 MVPs, 13 All-NBA First Team selections, and 5 All-Defensive First Team selections [lebron_accolades_160, lebron_accolades_320].
  * Jordan has at least 179 playoff games [jordan_playoffs_2560]; LeBron’s Cavaliers–Heat 8-year playoff peak outperformed Jordan’s Bulls in an 8-year normalized metric [jordan_defense_4480].
* **Subjective Judgments:**
  * The assertion that lifting an offense by 5 to 6 points is inherently *"GOAT-worthy"* is a subjective editorial characterization made in the text [jordan_defense_3120].
  * Deciding whether a higher scoring peak (Jordan) or sustained multi-decade All-NBA longevity and playmaking versatility (LeBron) constitutes the "GOAT" is an interpretative, subjective judgment rather than an empirical fact.
